title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 29
paragraphs: when these, I say, had been subdued and while he was still extending his Lydian dominion, there came to Sardis — which was then at the height of its wealth — all the wise men of Hellas who happened to be alive at the time, each brought there for his own reason. Among them was Solon the Athenian, who, after making laws for the Athenians at their request, had left his native country for ten years and sailed away, saying that he wanted to see various lands, so that he would not be forced to repeal any of the laws he had proposed. For the Athenians on their own could not do so, since they had bound themselves with solemn oaths to live for ten years under the laws Solon had made for them.
